subject: Acceptance criteria and staging network constraints for CedarBridge private deployment
messages:
From: CedarBridge Procurement <procurement@cedarbridge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Wilson <sara.wilson@cedarbridge.com>, Dr. Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@cedarbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: staging environment acceptance criteria

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the SOW draft — procurement and the security team reviewed and had a few staging-specific items we need clarified before we can sign off:  

1) We require an isolated staging VPC that mirrors our on-prem network reachability (no outbound internet by default). Please confirm how Redwood will support an air-gapped staging lane and whether you require a jump host for operator access.

2) Acceptance tests: CedarBridge needs a concrete smoke-test checklist and pass/fail thresholds for tokenization, inference latency (p95), and operator failover. Can you confirm Redwood will run the first three smoke-test runs and deliver results?

3) Patch/maintenance windows: we need guaranteed maintenance windows for staging that do not overlap with our ETL windows (daily 01:30-03:00 UTC). Provide your recommended SLAs for patch notice and rollback.

We attached the procurement checklist previously; happy to jump on a 30-minute call.

Best,
Procurement Team
CedarBridge Health

---
Attachments: procurement-checklist.xlsx (referenced)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: CedarBridge Procurement <procurement@cedarbridge.com>, Sara Wilson <sara.wilson@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: staging environment acceptance criteria

Sara / Procurement — thanks, this is really helpful context. High level responses below; detailed attachments and a proposed acceptance checklist are included in the SOW v3 I’m sharing.

- Air-gapped staging lane: Redwood can deploy a dedicated staging VPC inside your environment (or inside a customer-managed VPC) with egress blocked by default. For operator access we support either (a) customer-managed bastion/jump host (preferred for full control) or (b) Redwood-managed ephemeral jump host that runs inside the staging VPC and is reachable only via your approved VPN endpoints. We recommend option (a) for CedarBridge.

- Smoke tests & metrics: Redwood will run the initial smoke-test suite (three consecutive runs during handoff) and provide raw logs + a pass/fail report. Proposed p95 inference latency threshold for your 1k token test profile: <= 350ms on the configured instance class; tokenization and output fidelity checks are included. See attached smoke-test-plan.xlsx.

- Maintenance windows: we will not schedule platform updates that impact staging during your ETL window (01:30–03:00 UTC). We provide a minimum 7-day notice for non-emergency maintenance and a 24-hour rollback target for any change that degrades acceptance criteria. SLA language is in SOW v3.

Next steps: 1) confirm whether you want a customer-managed bastion; 2) approve the acceptance checklist in SOW v3; 3) schedule a 60-minute staging walkthrough next week so engineering can validate network flows.

I’m copying Rishi and Vanessa to coordinate the walkthrough and confirm the operator training plan.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CBH-SOW-v3.pdf; staging-network-diagram.png; smoke-test-plan.xlsx

Kim / team — quick internal notes so we show up prepared on the walkthrough:  

- If CedarBridge picks customer-managed bastion we need the bastion IP/range and allowlist ahead of time. Ask them for jump-host playbook and expected SSO/OAuth provider so we can pre-configure SAML connectors.

- For smoke tests, operations will need a sanitized sample dataset from CedarBridge (PII scrubbed) and an ingest manifest. If they cannot provide sanitized data we will run synthetic parity tests but will flag limitations in the acceptance report.

- Patch windows: legal may request language about emergency patches — propose we allow emergency security pushes with immediate notification and a 4-hour rollback SLA if requested.

I’ll draft the walkthrough agenda and an operator training checklist and drop into the Drive link Kim provided.

—Rishi
